newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal seen cutting rates Friday - poll.
newsitem.headline: Portugal seen cutting rates Friday - poll.

text.p: Nine out of 10 analysts polled by Reuters on Thursday expected the Bank of Portugal to cut interest rates when it announces terms for the next commercial bank reserve period on Friday.

They saw the repurchase pact rate being cut 20 to 30 basis points from its current 6.5 percent. The 6.2 percent drain rate -- the level at which the Bank absorbs market funds -- was seen being cut 20 to 50 basis points, while the emergency lending rate was expected to be lowered between 20 and 75 basis points from its current 8.3 percent.
The following is a table of analysts' forecasts (expressed as number of basis points -- bps -- to be cut from rate) Bank/brokerage Repo rate Drain rate Emergency lending
The sole analyst from a Portuguese bank who did not expect a rate cut declined to be identified for the poll.

The full names of the institutions taking part in the survey are as follows: ABN-AMRO Bank, Banco Finantia, Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI), Banco Mello de Investimentos (BMI), Banco de Comercio & Industria (BCI), Credit Lyonnais, Banco ESSI, IMF-Informacao de Mercados Financeiros, Siemca-Sociedade Mediadora de Capitais.
